body.one_liner: Shopify is a high-quality compounder with a strong growth-and-profitability profile (composite 6.9/10), but intangible-capital restatement reveals meaningfully lower economic ROIC than GAAP suggests, and several framework signals remain only partial — warranting a watchlist stance with active monitoring of moat durability and capital efficiency.

bull.headline: Exceptional growth-quality fundamentals: high-teen FCF margin, 19% GAAP ROIC, zero leverage, founder-CEO
bull.detail: F5 scores 8.5/10 (strong_fit): revenue CAGR of +27.3% over 3 years, FCF margin of +17.7%, GAAP ROIC of +19.2%, and debt/EBITDA of 0.0 — a rare combination of growth, profitability, and balance-sheet integrity. Tobias Lutke's founder-aligned classification reinforces Outsiders-style capital stewardship: over 6% equity ownership creates durable skin-in-the-game incentives. This profile is the central pillar of the hold-forever case.

bull.headline: Rule of 40 at 47.5 confirms the growth-profitability trade-off is favourable at scale
bull.detail: F6 captures a Rule of 40 score of 47.5 — above the conventional threshold — alongside a GP/A band in the top 40th percentile proxy and a diversified customer base. The Fahlenbrach founder signal fires positive. These signals collectively indicate that Shopify's platform economics are not deteriorating as the business scales, a key durability condition for a platform compounder thesis.

bull.headline: Piotroski 7/9 and Sloan high-quality accruals signal financial statement integrity
bull.detail: F1 returns 6.17/10 with a Piotroski score of 7/9 and the Sloan accrual quality flag set to True — indicating that reported earnings are substantially backed by cash flows rather than accrual inflation. Asset growth is in the low-positive band, reducing the risk of empire-building dilution. These signals reduce the probability of accounting-quality deterioration that would undermine the long-term compounding thesis.

bull.headline: Moderate-winner BEW candidate: profile warrants a sized, extended hold position
bull.detail: The BEW overlay resolves to moderate_winner_candidate. Bessembinder's research establishes that extreme compounding in equity returns is concentrated in a small subset of stocks, and under-sizing or premature trimming of those positions is the dominant source of portfolio wealth destruction. A composite of 6.9/10 with an F5 strong_fit and a founder-CEO with substantial equity is the profile base rate for multi-year compounders — the hold-forever default is structurally supported.

bull.headline: PEAD positive drift and proximity to 52-week high suggest market is not pricing in deterioration
bull.detail: F2 (Momentum, 6.0/10) shows a positive post-earnings announcement drift signal alongside a price sitting near the 52-week high (+3.0% from peak). The trailing 12-1 momentum reads at -12.9%, indicating near-term price softness that has not broken the longer-term uptrend. For a long-horizon holder, this pattern is consistent with re-accumulation rather than distribution — not an actionable signal but not a warning sign either.

bear.headline: Peters-Taylor economic ROIC of 9.6% is materially below GAAP ROIC of 15.2% — capital efficiency is overstated
bear.detail: The ICA-5 overlay fires on a 5.56pp gap between GAAP ROIC (15.19%) and Peters-Taylor-adjusted ROIC (9.63%), directionally downward. Once R&D and 25% of SG&A are capitalised as economically durable assets, the invested capital base expands substantially — compressing the true return on invested capital. For a business spending over 13% of revenue on R&D, this restatement is not cosmetic. The hold thesis must be grounded in the economic ROIC trajectory, not the GAAP figure.

bear.headline: Gross margin has contracted an average of 91 bps/year — scale is not producing margin expansion
bear.detail: F3 (Innovation Compounder, 4.0/10) flags average gross margin expansion of -91.0 bps/year. This is contrary to the expectation for a platform business: scale should widen margins via operating leverage on fixed infrastructure. Sustained margin contraction at the gross level may reflect merchant solutions mix-shift toward lower-margin payments and logistics, or competitive pricing pressure on subscription tiers. This is the most important second-order signal to monitor across the next several annual filings.

bear.headline: NRR and GRR not publicly disclosed — retention quality of the merchant base is unobservable
bear.detail: F6 records NRR and GRR as not_disclosed. For a platform business, net and gross revenue retention are the single most important metrics for assessing whether the installed base is expanding or eroding. Their absence from 10-K MD&A means the compounding thesis rests on revenue CAGR and Rule of 40 without confirmation that cohort-level economics are sound. A challenger displacing existing merchants would show up in these metrics first — and they are currently blind.

bear.headline: F4 partially blind: options flow absent, short data withheld — stealth accumulation signal is degraded
bear.detail: F4 scores 4.5/10 with no Form 4 insider transactions found on EDGAR, no open-market buyers in the 90-day window, and both short interest (current and peak) withheld due to third-party data restrictions. The options put/call ratio was skipped due to data availability. The decline signal does not fire and EPS acceleration is characterised as net_increase_with_dips, but the overall F4 read is structurally incomplete. Institutional behaviour and insider conviction signals cannot be assessed.

bear.headline: F7 (Smart Beta Timing) unfeasible — only 7 annual periods available; cycle-calibrated valuation anchor absent
bear.detail: PSA-3 fires: F7 requires 10 annual periods; Shopify's public listing (May 2015) provides only 7. This means the cycle-aware valuation timing framework is entirely absent from the composite. The composite score of 6.9/10 is therefore weighted across F1–F6 only, with F5 carrying 37.5% of the weight. Absence of F7 removes the single framework most likely to flag overvaluation relative to historical trading ranges — a material blind spot given the growth premium embedded in the price.

risks.factor: Monitor whether Peters-Taylor economic ROIC (currently 9.6%) converges toward or diverges further from GAAP ROIC over 2–3 more annual filings. Sustained divergence above 3pp implies the business is deploying intangible capital at sub-optimal rates — a thesis-break condition if economic ROIC trends below cost of capital.

Monitor gross margin trajectory across next 3 annual filings. If the -91 bps/year contraction trend continues without an offsetting mix-shift explanation (e.g. payments volume growing faster than subscription, with explicit margin disclosure), it signals structural pricing pressure or adverse mix that undermines platform compounding.

Monitor whether Shopify begins disclosing NRR/GRR in 10-K MD&A. Persistent non-disclosure of retention metrics for a merchant platform prevents assessment of cohort-level economics and is a structural information gap in the moat validation process.

Monitor the Rule of 40 score across annual filings as revenue growth moderates at scale. A sustained decline below the 40 threshold would signal that the growth-profitability trade-off is deteriorating, weakening the platform compounder thesis.

Monitor for any reversion in founder-CEO alignment: dilutive share issuance patterns, SBC acceleration relative to revenue growth, or reduction in Lutke's economic ownership below current levels. Capital allocator drift is a Buffett/Thorndike thesis-break condition.

Monitor whether Form 4 insider transaction data becomes available on EDGAR. Current absence of insider open-market purchases (0 buyers in the 90-day window) combined with no Form 4 activity leaves conviction signals from management unverifiable.

Monitor for F4 options put/call data becoming available. Current PSA-3 trigger reflects F7 data immaturity (137 months since listing, still short of the 10-year requirement). As the history window extends, F7 will become feasible and may materially alter the composite — watch for cycle-valuation signals when F7 activates.

data_caveats: No Form 4 insider transactions were found on EDGAR for SHOP; insider conviction and open-market purchase signals are unverifiable for this run.
F4 options put/call ratio was not computed — no free-tier data source was available per project specification; the F4 stealth-accumulation signal is structurally incomplete.
F5 buyback yield could not be computed — market cap and share repurchase data were not persisted; capital return signals via buyback are absent.
F6 NRR and GRR are recorded as not_disclosed — Shopify's 10-K MD&A does not report these retention metrics; cohort-level revenue quality is unobservable from public filings.

F7 (Smart Beta Timing) is unfeasible due to insufficient annual history (7 periods available; 10 required); the cycle-calibrated valuation timing signal is entirely absent from the composite for this run.
